raw_response:
I am old now, 72, and only one person in the house, so I cannot toss money around or do heavy work too many times. On this 1.2 mu I will still do the wheat-maize rotation, same as most people here. That is the safest way for me. Wheat gives steady grain, and maize follows right after, so even if one season is not so good, I still have the other. I finished many years on this land, so I do not like making big changes. The extension people talk about precise rates, but on such a small plot I mainly look at what worked before, what my neighbors are doing, and how much cash I can spare. I have well water, so if it turns dry I can still save the crop, but pumping costs money, so I will not irrigate more than needed.

For wheat, I will sow in early October with a common improved local variety that is easy to buy in the village. I will put base fertilizer first, then one topdress around jointing if the stand looks all right. I do not want wheat to go yellow, so I would rather put a little extra nitrogen than too little, but I still keep it moderate because fertilizer is expensive. I will irrigate around sowing if soil moisture is short, then at overwintering or jointing, and once around grain filling only if the spring is dry. After wheat harvest in June, I will not do deep tillage because the turnaround is too tight and I am too old for extra field work. I will clear the straw simply and seed maize quickly. For maize I will use a hybrid seed, put most fertilizer at planting, then maybe a small topdress if the crop looks weak after knee-high stage. If rain is normal, one irrigation is enough, maybe none; if summer turns dry, I will irrigate once or twice because missing maize at tasseling hurts yield badly.
